# `Q-9-11` — Missing Text Source

> A `<cs:text>` element does not specify any source for the
> text it should render.

## What this means

The CSL `<cs:text>` element renders text drawn from one of four
sources, selected by exactly one of these attributes:
`variable` (a citation field like `title` or `author`),
`macro` (the name of another macro), `term` (a CSL localized
term), or `value` (a literal string). The element must specify
exactly one. This error fires when it specifies none.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A hand-edited `<cs:text>`** where the source attribute was
  deleted but the element itself was kept.
- **A typo** in the attribute name — `varaible="..."` instead
  of `variable="..."` — so the parser sees the attribute as
  unknown and the element as without a source.

## How to fix

Add one of the four source attributes. Pick the one that
matches what the text should render: a field from the citation
(`variable`), the result of another macro (`macro`), a
localized term (`term`), or a literal string (`value`).

## Related

- `Q-9-7` — required attribute missing: the same family of
  error, for elements that require a specific attribute (as
  opposed to "one of these four").
